selected_evidence.requirement: node2's port-8080 service exists and is reachable only from node1 (private-network premise)
selected_evidence.summary: Created and started the node2 HTTP service (systemd unit, port 8080), restricted node2 firewalld to accept 8080 only from node1's IP; verified node1 can reach node2:8080 while node3 directly cannot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Publish node2:8080 on node1's management address (10.100.63.10) port 80
selected_evidence.summary: Freed port 80 by disabling OPNsense's http->https webGUI redirect, added NAT rdr rule (lan:80 -> 10.100.63.11:8080), reloaded the filter, and confirmed via pfctl -s nat that the rdr rule is active and port 80 is free.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 can reach the published port and receives node2's content
selected_evidence.summary: After scoping the hairpin SNAT and filter rules to the post-NAT destination (10.100.63.11:8080), repeated curl tests from node3 to http://10.100.63.10:80/ return HTTP 200 with node2's actual content, confirmed stable across 3 repeated tries.

selected_evidence.requirement: The published port stays refused for every other source address
selected_evidence.summary: curl from node2 and from node1 itself to 10.100.63.10:80 returns exit code 7 'Connection refused' in ~4-6ms (immediate RST, not a timeout); pf rule hit counters confirm the reject rule (block return quick) is actually matching and counting packets/hits for these refused sources.

selected_evidence.requirement: Root-cause diagnosis and correct fix for the hairpin/NAT-filter matching problem
selected_evidence.summary: Diagnosed and fixed multiple issues in sequence: global disablenatreflection blocking per-rule reflection; natreflection=purenat causing pf to bind filter rules to the wrong indexed interface address (vtnet0:1); and finally confirmed pf filters on the POST-NAT destination, requiring filter rules to match 10.100.63.11:8080 rather than the pre-NAT 10.100.63.10:80.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline kern.boottime, issued backgrounded /sbin/reboot (ack returned before disconnect), observed SSH timeout then successful reconnect with kern.boottime changed from 1788629485 to 1788630467, and confirmed pf rules/services and full functional test (node3 pass, node2 refused) recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (6aa805ba...), issued backgrounded systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id (c7ea9946...) and fresh uptime, verified node2-webapp systemd service and firewalld rich rule persisted, and confirmed the full access-control test still passes after this restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (c2f29441...), issued backgrounded systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id (a4e8ffb5...) and fresh uptime, then re-verified end-to-end: node3 gets HTTP 200 with node2's content, node2-as-source is still refused.
